uncited: It differs from general multivariate transfer functions by utilizing a subspace-aware ID map to handle overlapping indexed points from different subspaces, distinguishing it from its sibling [Rendering Continuous Indexed Points](14769-rendering-continuous-indexed-points.md) which focuses on the rasterization of the points themselves rather than the transfer function logic.
*   **Input:** Volumetric sample value at spatial location $\mathbf{x}$; precomputed indexed point volume; ID map; color and opacity maps; subspace ID ($sID$); transfer function ID ($tID$).
**Indexed Point Volume:** A 3D volume where each voxel stores the 2D indexed point location $\eta$ corresponding to the spatial location $\mathbf{x}$.
*   Subspace ID ($sID$): Distinguishes subspaces in overlapping regions.
*   Transfer Function ID ($tID$): Identifies and links specific transfer functions.
**Retrieve Indexed Point:** Look up the precomputed indexed point location $\eta$ from the Indexed Point Volume at $\mathbf{x}$.
*   **Performance:** Computing the transformation from local fitting information $(\xi, \mathbf{X})$ to $\eta$ for every fragment is costly.
*   **Overlapping Subspaces:** Indexed points of positive correlations may overlap with neighboring subspaces.
*   **Precomputation:** The time to compute indexed points volumes depends on the subdivision threshold ($t_s$), eigenvector interpolation threshold ($t_e$), and dataset noise.
